episodes.215608: A storm system moved into the area from the northern Rockies, generating some strong thunderstorms, some of which became severe as they moved from central Montana through northeast Montana.
episodes.216228: A cold front stalled across Eastern North Carolina during the afternoon hours of August twenty-third. This combined with ample instability and wind shear over the Carolinas resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms developing along and out ahead of this front across the Coastal Plain. This activity then tracked east with a few of these storms becoming severe in nature bringing strong wind gusts to portions of the inland rivers, Pamlico Sound, Core Sound, and coastal waters north of Cape Hatteras during the afternoon and evening of August twenty-third.
episodes.216230: A stalled front remained across the Inner Banks of Eastern North Carolina on August twenty-fourth and was the focal point for scattered shower and thunderstorm development during the afternoon hours. Enough instability was in place for a few storms to become severe in nature bringing strong wind gusts to portions of the Neuse River, Core Banks, Pamlico Sound, and coastal waters south of Cape Hatteras. Shower and thunderstorm activity quickly dissipated after sunset with the loss of daytime heating.
episodes.216295: A stalled front draped across the Inner Banks of eastern North Carolina was the focal point for scattered shower and thunderstorm development during the afternoon hours. Several clusters of storms became severe and produced wind damage. A tornado briefly touched down in the open marshlands of Cedar Island.
episodes.216575: Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms produced a few wind gusts in excess of 34 knots and a waterspout off the coast of Port St Joe.
episodes.216593: A stalled frontal boundary was positioned over the Sandhills and central Coastal Plain of central North Carolina. A wave of low pressure tracked along the front during the early morning hours, producing isolated wind damage reports across Cumberland, Scotland, and Hoke Counties.
episodes.216852: A complex of strong to severe thunderstorms developed over Pima County in southern AZ during the late afternoon/early evening hours, fueled by over 1000 J/KG of MLCAPE. With DCAPE values of 1500-2000 J/KG, the environment was very conducive for strong downburst winds, resulting in organized outflows. As the complex of thunderstorms continued to mature as it migrated northward from Pima into Pinal County, an organized outflow materialized and moved northward through much of south-central AZ, resulting in dense blowing dust with widespread visibility reductions of under one mile reported. A major dust storm-related accident occurred along I-8 near Mile Post 172 as a commercial vehicle rear ended a trailer of another commercial vehicle causing severe injuries to the driver and entrapping him in his vehicle.  Although scattered showers and thunderstorms continued into the overnight hours, not much in the way of impacts were reported with the exception of State Route 238 near mobile, where over an inch of rain in less than one hour fell, forcing the closure of the Highway due to flooding.
episodes.216947: Afternoon thunderstorm over northwestern Puerto Rico produced excessive rainfall that led to a landslide in Aguada.
episodes.217013: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.
episodes.217540: A funnel cloud was sighted near Myrtle Beach Airport.
episodes.217542: Three quarter inch hail fell north of Wilmington, NC.
episodes.217731: A broad sub-tropical ridge axis was centered to the west of the area over Texas and the southern Plains resulting in a deep layer northerly flow regime in the mid and upper levels of the atmosphere. Additionally, a stationary front extended east-southeastward from central Louisiana toward Lower Alabama across southwest Mississippi.  A line of of strong to severe thunderstorms developed along the stationary frontal boundary over southwest Mississippi and then swept southward through southeast Louisiana  during the afternoon  hours. The severe storms within the line produced severe wind gusts.
episodes.217732: A broad sub-tropical ridge axis was centered to the west of the area over Texas and the southern Plains resulting in a deep layer northerly flow regime in the mid and upper levels of the atmosphere. Additionally, a stationary front extended east-southeastward from central Louisiana toward Lower Alabama across southwest Mississippi. A line of of strong to severe thunderstorms developed along the stationary frontal boundary over southwest Mississippi and then swept southward across Lake Pontchartrain and the Mississippi Sound in the afternoon hours. The severe storms within the line produced severe wind gusts over the waters.
episodes.217858: A shortwave trough moved across the northern rockies, causing the high pressure to shift back westward. Deep monsoonal moisture in place and the forcing from this shortwave trough resulted in thunderstorm development with heavy rainfall causing flash flooding and debris flows mainly impacting the burn scar areas, particularly the Gold Mountain Burn Scar and Lee Burn Scar. Storms training over the Lee Burn Scar in particular resulted in debris flows and mudslides both on the 23rd and 24th of August.
episodes.217885: A series of showers and thunderstorms formed along a weak front moving west to east across the northern half of the Texas Panhandle during the afternoon and evening of the 23rd. Most of this activity was non-severe, but a few cells manage to generate downdrafts strong enough to produce severe wind gusts. A heat burst even occurred during the night time hours, but no thunder was associated with this wind gust.
episodes.217939: A thunderstorm produced a localized microburst and localized wind damage north of Minnewaukan, ND during the early morning hours.
episodes.217940: A frontal boundary dropped southward into southern GA on the 24th before stalling into the 25th. This, combined with some weak upper level energy and influences from southwest flow and the Atlantic sea breeze, resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms and isolated strong to severe cells across northeast FL. Impacts were mainly due to heavy rainfall from slow moving storms, though isolated thunderstorm wind damage also occurred.
episodes.218188: A line of showers and thunderstorms moved through western and central North Dakota during the afternoon and evening along a surface trough, with a few scattered severe reports coming from Billings, Ward, and Dunn Counties. The largest hail of 1.5 inches in diameter was reported in Billings County west of Medora, and damaging thunderstorm wind gusts were estimated up to 70 mph in Dunn County east of Mandaree.
episodes.218189: A surface trough pushed east through the state during the afternoon and evening, with the center of the low traversing the southern Canadian Prairies. A cluster of supercells developed and produced large hail in the northern James River Valley, before consolidating into a line as they moved south and produced damaging thunderstorm wind gusts in McIntosh County. The strongest measured wind gust was 77 mph in Wishek, and the largest hail was 1.5 inches in diameter near Woodworth in Stutsman County.
episodes.218201: An isolated severe weather event occurred on August 23rd as a mid-level shortwave trough moved through the Great Lakes region that evening. Afternoon showers and thunderstorms limited the instability across the region, though there still was around 500 J/kg of MLCAPE along with modest low level lapse rates. Bulk shear was sufficient as well around 40-50 knots.
episodes.218206: Following the cold front on the 22nd, a trailing surface trough axis crossed Lake Erie during the evening hours of the 23rd. The warm waters of Lake Erie helped a modest amount of instability develop over the lake, with relatively strong winds in place aloft. This allowed thunderstorms that swept across the lake along the trough to produce strong, gusty winds, particularly in the waters offshore of the Cleveland area.
episodes.218209: A weak shortwave tracking across a moderately unstable airmass displaying steep low-level lapse rates and large downdraft cape supported thunderstorms capable of damaging winds.
episodes.218210: A weak shortwave tracking across a moderately unstable airmass displaying steep low-level lapse rates and large downdraft cape supported thunderstorms capable of damaging winds.
episodes.218222: On August 21st and 22nd, a mid level shortwave moved through southeast Georgia and interacted with sea breeze and outflow boundaries to produce scattered to numerous showers and storms. Cooler than normal temperatures aloft from -7C to -8C at 500 mb increased mid level lapse rates which supported a couple of strong to severe thunderstorms. Another frontal boundary dropped southward into northern GA on the 23rd, into southern GA on the 24th before stalling into the 25th. This, combined with some weak upper level energy and influences from southwest flow and the Atlantic sea breeze, resulted in numerous showers and thunderstorms and isolated strong to severe cells.
episodes.218227: A heat wave developed across the region during late August. A weak boundary and short wave approached from the north causing strong to severe storms.
episodes.218267: Strong to severe thunderstorms brought all modes of severe weather, including a reported tornado.
episodes.218310: Warm front moves through Maine on Monday morning, August 24th, with a slow moving cold front swinging through mid-day into the evening. Marine layer sets up over Downeast region, preventing the region from developing strong storms. Storms developed in northern, Central Highlands, and Bangor regions along the frontal boundary. Some storms developed enough to have gusty winds, particularly in the Piscataquis region. Storms began to weaken by nighttime.
episodes.218478: The subtropical ridge established itself once again with weak troughing off the Pacific Northwestern U.S. coastline. With robust moisture return in place, this would set the stage for flash flooding across southern Utah and scattered instances of severe thunderstorms producing severe wind gusts across northern Utah.
episodes.218488: Rugby experienced significant flooding on the western part of town, with flooding reported in numerous basements and water covering some roadways. A deep upper level low tracked through the Canadian Prairies, while a surface trough and attendant low moved through North Dakota. Areas of slow-moving thunderstorms that were efficient rain producers progressed northwest to southeast, re-developing and training over the same area, and led to bouts of torrential rain over parts of Pierce County. ||With these thunderstorms, there was also one report of damaging thunderstorm winds, with a 58 mph gust measured near Ray.

events.narrative: Pierce County Emergency Manager reported that numerous homes had flooding in their basements due to the torrential rain that had fallen the evening of the 23rd into the morning of the 24th, including her own. There was street flooding that was focused on the western side of the town of Rugby. The morning of the 24th, there was standing water across one of the mobile home parks in town. The highest report relayed was 8.74 inches of rain, measured just north of the new Rugby hospital. There was also a report of 7 inches of rain from just west of Rugby.
